hook: A five-strain E. coli community learns an association, holds it as memory, and erases it on command.
summary: Five engineered E. coli strains share one quorum-sensing signal that serves as the memory, and together they showed classic associative learning: after pairing, a stimulus that was silent before triggered a response. The memory survived a medium exchange and could be erased. It is a lab demonstration in a culture with a simple model, not a durable or general memory system.
title: Associative Learning and Memory Erasure in a Synthetic Multicellular System
